label: GO step after a rewarded trial, agent strongly choosing a1
explanation: Fires only at the GO step (never D1 or D2), only when the previous trial was rewarded (prev_reward == 1; never after unrewarded trials), and only when the agent is about to choose a1 (99.96% of activations have action == 1; model_act == 1 on all of them). The agent policy logit choice > 5 (strong a1 preference) is the cleanest condition (dev F1 0.99). The upcoming-choice version (phase == GO) & (prev_reward == 1) & (action == 1) reaches F1 0.93; action is the agent own upcoming choice, which is legitimate, but I recorded the policy-logit version because it is observable at the step and more precise. No future random outcome is needed. Its false positives are mostly GO steps after a reward where a1 is chosen with a weaker logit. It is silent on a2 choices and on all non-GO steps. Magnitude: example windows suggest activation is highest early in a run of rewarded a1 choices (often right after a rare/unrewarded trial) and shrinks over long uninterrupted streaks; choice > 8.07 alone gives precision 1.0. I did not quantify this further.

issues: Every factual claim held up on the test split. The feature never fires outside GO (phase != GO gives F1 0). It never fires after an unrewarded trial ((GO) & (prev_reward == 0) gives F1 0). It almost never fires on a2 choices ((GO) & (action == 2) gives recall 0.0004). The original predicate scores P 0.985, R 0.998, F1 0.992. The action == 1 version scores F1 0.928. choice > 8.07 with GO and prev_reward == 1 gives precision 1.0 but recall only 0.83.

Small refinement, not a refutation: in the profile, almost all activations follow a previous a1 choice or the first trial of a window (prev_action == 2 holds only 0.2% of mass). This is mostly already captured by choice > 5, because a rewarded a2 trial seldom produces a strong a1 logit. Adding prev_action != 2 gives test F1 0.988, so the label does not need to change. In misses, some false positives are switches from a2 back to a1.

Misses on the test split: 155 missed steps holding 0.0% of activation mass, all at GO with prev_reward == 1 and a weaker a1 logit. False positives: 1573 steps, scattered, mostly GO after a reward where a1 has a high logit but the feature is silent. I found no systematic class (phase, position, transition or good state) among them.
The magnitude claim (strongest early in a run of rewarded a1 choices) was not measured. It is hedged as anecdotal, so it is not counted against the label.
The predicate uses no future variable. choice is the agent's own policy logit, which is legitimate.
